 Analysis Week 7 NFL MVP tracker: Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III making legitimate case; Bryce Young enters top 5
 Published: Loading... Kevin Patra Senior News Writer Share Facebook Share Twitter If we wanted more accurate seasonal awards, we’d rename the NFL MVP the Top QB of the Year Award.
 Over the past 13 years, a quarterback has won the MVP. It marks the longest streak of one position taking home the trophy since the 1970 merger.
 By far.
 Before voters essentially decided that MVP was a QB honor, no position won the trophy for more than five consecutive seasons (2007-2011).
 QBs have taken home 18 of the past 19 MVP awards, with only Adrian Peterson's memorable 2,097-yard rushing season with the 2012 Vikings breaking the string.
 It’s slightly obtuse that the MVP award has morphed into a QB trophy while the rest of the league is relegated to squabbling over Offensive or Defensive Player of the Year as their de facto top honor.
 I get it. Quarterbacks play the most difficult position in sports. They must manage games with a different level of mental acuity and perform feats of physical absurdity. They also must carry themselves like a Fortune 500 CEO, but without the stuffy arrogance that would alienate a fan base. The upper echelon deserves to be honored.
 The question now is if any other position has even a remote shot at breaking the QB blockade on the MVP award. Running backs are realistically the only ones with a shot to do so, but even an illustrious 2,000-yard rushing season no longer seems to generate a sniff. In 2024, Saquon Barkley scampered for 2,005 yards , electing to sit out the 17th game rather than chase Eric Dickerson’s record of 2,105 yards set in 16 games in 1984. For his efforts on a division champion squad, Barkley  didn't receive a single first-place MVP vote . He finished a distant third behind Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson . At least Saquon got some votes.
 Loading... Watch highlights of Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley during the 2024 NFL season.
 In 2020, under the old voting method in which people only casted a single ballot,  Derrick Henry ’s 2,027-yard campaign for a first-place Titans squad didn’t garner any MVP votes. Zero.
 We don’t even have to pretend a receiver, defensive player, or -- LOL -- a lineman has a snowball's chance in Hades of taking the MVP stage.
 The hilariously low odds of even a running back knocking off the QB streak bring us to Kenneth Walker III .
 The  reigning Super Bowl MVP running back is on a streak of terror in Kansas City.
 Despite playing one game fewer (five) than most backs due to an early bye week, Walker leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards. He leads the NFL with 6.3 yards per attempt, and his 133 yards per game is on pace to blast past Dickerson’s single-season rushing record -- during which the Hall of Famer averaged 131.6 YPG over 16 tilts. (I should point out that Dickerson finished second in MVP voting that year to Dan Marino’s 5,000-yard passing campaign). 
 Walker had two touchdowns in the Chiefs' Week 6 win over the Chargers, his fourth multi-touchdown game this season, joining Calvin Johnson Jr. (2011) as the only players since the 1970 merger to score multiple TDs in four of their first five games of a season.
 Walker has been the league's best running back, and when it comes to advanced metrics, it’s not particularly close. Per Next Gen Stats, the K.C. beast has generated 277 rushing yards over expected -- more than 100 clear of the next-closest player ( Bijan Robinson at 170). His 13.2 rush EPA is nearly double No. 2 ( Christian McCaffrey at 6.8). And his EPA per carry of 0.12 is better than all comers (CMC second at 0.09).
 Walker’s tackle-breaking ability has been ridiculous. He's generated 47 missed tackles forced, most in the league (per NGS), and his 275 MTF yards are also tops.
 Loading... Highlights from Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III during Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season where he gained 128 yards on the ground and scored two touchdowns on the ground.
 The running back has been the most vital player on a team that includes Patrick Mahomes . His penchant for creating a game-tilting big play has spearheaded the Chiefs' 5-0 start, including touchdown runs of 60 , 33 and 22 yards . Mahomes, meanwhile, hasn’t thrown a TD pass longer than 13 yards this season.
 Despite all the data suggesting K9 is off to an MVP-caliber start, Vegas doesn’t give the running back much of a chance to win the award. He currently sits at +7500, behind 13 QBs and Jahmyr Gibbs (+4000), per FanDuel.
 Multiple things are going to have to happen for Walker to bust up the QB siege. No. 1, he’ll almost certainly have to break Dickerson’s record. No. 2, Brock Purdy will have to nosedive from his hot start, Josh Allen has to throw some late-season head-scratching interceptions in prime time, and no other QB can surge ahead of the pack. No. 3, voters will have to decide they hate the quarterback-award narrative and collectively give it to an RB.
 That’s a lot that must go in Walker’s favor. Only one of which he has control over.
 Personally, I think it’s clear Walker has easily been among the top five most valuable players through six weeks. That’s why he’ll remain high in my rankings despite what the odds might suggest. But no, sadly, I don’t foresee an NFL MVP in Walker’s future. He’d probably settle for a shot at back-to-back Super Bowl MVP awards, though.

Oct 19, 2026 MVP RANKINGS
 NOTE: Up/down arrows below reflect movement from the Week 6 edition . 
 1 — No Rank change Brock Purdy SF QB Purdy came back toward the pack with a rough second half on Monday night . That will happen when you’re playing without your top six receivers. Still, the undefeated QB remains atop my rankings. He showed in the first half that when he has at least one superior pass catcher, he can carve up a defense. He reiterated that while not a prolific scrambler, his runs are crucial to keeping drives alive. Purdy still sits No. 1 in EPA per dropback, success rate, and first down percent among QBs with at least 100 attempts, per Next Gen Stats.
 2 Caret Up Rank increased by 2 Kenneth Walker III KC RB See above. He’s the leading reason the Chiefs are 5-0.
 3 Caret Down Rank decreased by 1 Josh Allen BUF QB Allen’s ridiculous touchdown flip on the run in Las Vegas last week was made for an MVP montage. The Bills QB is pushing Purdy, moving within a point of the 49ers passer in EPA per dropback (0.29), and his 229.1% win probability added is nearly 100 points ahead of No. 2 ( C.J. Stroud , 131.4%). Allen is on the move. It wouldn’t shock me at all if he is atop this list within the next month. 
 Loading... Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen's best plays from 255-yard game vs. Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6.
 4 Caret Down Rank decreased by 1 Trevor Lawrence JAX QB If not for a few crucial turnovers, Lawrence could have his Jags undefeated and at the top of this list. The QB threw a ghastly red zone INT in the first half in London but remains an efficient passer, ranking fourth in EPA per dropback (0.21). Lawrence has authored some of the season's most impressive tight window passes. If he wasn’t playing this well, the Jags would be hanging out under .500 like the rest of the AFC South. Against man coverage, Lawrence went 9 of 13 for 115 yards and three touchdowns against the Texans, tying his career high for TDs against man coverage in a game.
 5 Caret Up Rank increased by NR Bryce Young CAR QB Bryce enters the chat. I don’t much care that Vegas gives Young worse odds than Gibbs. That’s simply a product, in my opinion, of the general public overlooking the Panthers. Young has been lethal through five games. If you’re looking for a long shot at this point, the 2023 No. 1 pick isn’t a bad dart throw. The QB is tied for sixth in EPA/dropback (0.15 with Mahomes). Young has been particularly deadly against five- and six-man rushes, as he's tied with Lamar Jackson for a league-best 0.36 EPA/DB against blitz looks (min. 25 attempts on such plays). It came down to Young versus Jordan Love for my final spot this week. The more efficient passer got the nod. If the Panthers keep racking up wins, their QB will get more national attention.
 Next in line: Packers QB Jordan Love, Texans QB C.J. Stroud, Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba , Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs, Lions QB Jared Goff
